feature: One shape for the capture history pane
summary: The capture history panel now looks the same everywhere the redline flow can reach it: a chromeless glass pane with a centered All / Screenshots / Videos filter, Clear All, and a strip of captures. The old version with a title bar and a close button is gone from the shell reference and from the measure and redline page.
setup: The design study, on the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8791. No app build needed.

try.do: Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/app-shell.html and scroll to the Capture history specimen.
Click Screenshots, then Videos, then All, and watch the strip filter.
Switch the dashboard to light theme and look at the same specimen again.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/redline.html and click the clock-arrow History button at the top right of the canvas.
Press Esc to put the pane away, then click the History button again and click anywhere on the capture to dismiss it.
Compare the two panes: they should read as the same surface in two places.

evaluate: With no title and no close button, is it still obvious what the pane is and how to put it away?
On the reference page the pane floats over a dark desktop plate; on the redline page it floats inside the editor window. Does that difference read as one surface, or as two?
The strip holds nine captures on the reference page and scrolls sideways. Is horizontal scrolling the right way to get to older captures, or do you want a grid?
The selected card is the only one showing copy, edit, pin and delete. Is one action row enough, or should hovering reveal them too?
Was the ruling right? A History button on a window is allowed, but it opens this one global pane and never a window-shaped copy of it.
rough: Thirty-six other study pages still draw the old title-bar-and-close-button version of this pane, about forty panes in all (editor, image, video, paint, typography, the lang-* and ui-* pages, and more). This task only covered the shell reference and the redline page. The rest is a corpus sweep worth doing.

On the redline page the pane hangs inside the editor window rather than over the desktop, because that page only draws a window. It matches what every other window-only page does, but a surface described as global sitting inside a window frame is still a small lie.
The scope filter is wired by hand in page code on redline and composites, while desk pages get it from the shared entry component. Same behavior, two implementations.

The shell reference page had a second, unreachable history pane hidden in its main window with nothing to open it. It was deleted rather than converted, so the page teaches the surface in exactly one place.
